pr_title: Ensure JsonTypeInfo does not fail configuration for valid metadata originating from fast-path sourcegen
pr_body:
Rearranges the configuration logic so that certain failure modes are surfaced at serialization time rather than configuration time.

Fix #72614.

issue_context.title: JsonTypeInfo generated using JsonSourceGenerationMode.Serialization throws NotSupportedException on configuration
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/area-system-text-json, @gregsdennis See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
Minimal reproduction ```C# using System; using System.Text.Json; using System.Text.Json.Serialization; using System.Text.Json.Serialization.Metadata; var options = new JsonSerializerOptions { TypeInfoResolver = JsonTypeInfoResolver.Combine(MyContext.Default) }; Console.WriteLine(JsonSerializer.Serialize(new MyPoco { Value = 42 }, options)); [JsonSerializable(typeof(MyPoco), GenerationMode = JsonSourceGenerationMode.Serialization)] public partial class MyContext : JsonSerializerContext { } public class MyPoco { public int Value { get; set; } } ``` Throws ``` Unhandled exception. System.InvalidOperationException: 'JsonSerializerContext' '' did not provide property metadata for type 'MyPoco'. at System.Text.Json.ThrowHelper.ThrowInvalidOperationException_NoMetadataForTypeProperties(JsonSerializerContext context, Type type) at System.Text.Json.Serialization.Metadata.SourceGenJsonTypeInfo`1.AddPropertiesUsingSourceGenInfo() at System.Text.Json.Serialization.Metadata.JsonTypeInfo.Configure() at System.Text.Json.Serialization.Metadata.JsonTypeInfo.EnsureConfigured() at System.Text.Json.JsonSerializerOptions.GetOrAddJsonTypeInfo(Type type) at System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer.GetTypeInfo(JsonSerializerOptions options, Type runtimeType) at System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer.Serialize[TValue](TValue value, JsonSerializerOptions options) ``` This should not throw during the configuration stage, since this is a valid representation of `JsonTypeInfo`. It should support serialization for root-level values of type MyPoco, but should throw an exception when serializing nested values of type `MyPoco` or when deserializing.
Author: eiriktsarpalis
Assignees: -
Labels: `area-System.Text.Json`
Milestone: -

review_comments: I think this should use generated options and ensure this throws when any setting is changed (since fast path should not be used then)
see next comment in this file for what I mean specifically
Makes sense, but currently this will always fail regardless of options configuration. For options with JsonSerializerContext specifically we already have test coverage for all those scenaria.

btw since we're micro optimizing we could technically change `HasSerializeHandler` into `CanUseFastPath` and combine `info.Options.SerializerContext?.CanUseSerializationLogic && jsonTypeInfo.HasSerializeHandler`
I think we could. I'll consider it for the fix for #72187
you might want to create similar test (i.e. change this into theory) where you change different setting like naming policy. We should also not use fast path in that case
I think it's something to consider once #71933 gets fixed. Currently it always fails so turning it into a theory wouldn't differentiate anything.

it does make a difference because of how me make the checks (i.e. if SerializerContext is null we always not use fast path but if it's not null we need to make sure we also respect the options). Also considering you're removing https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/72630#discussion_r927419181 which checks exactly that I'd consider that even more important that we do the right thing
Maybe, I'll add this in the upcoming PR for https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/71933 (which is blocked by this change) to avoid triggering another CI cycle. Let's get this merged for now.
I'm actually curious, can this check ever not be true?

Currently, yes. It can be `JsonTypeInfo<SomeOtherType>` because of polymorphism. I was planning on changing that as part of a fix for #72187 but then I hit this bug. I will change in a second iteration.

I think this check was correct before and I think we should do that in other places as well. Basically SerializeHandler is currently always ignored unless the other check is true. This might be another reason to merge `SerializeHandler` and `context?.CanUseSerializationLogic == true` into `CanUseFastPath`
Can you elaborate on resolving this?

Regarding

> I think this check was correct before and I think we should do that in other places as well.

Nothing really changes, since the `context?.CanUseSerializationLogic == true` check is also done before the call to https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/72630/files#diff-43fe82ce53bba0eb09ea1dfdcd1f8774473c177831110a2cfc2a83979e9b7e11R83 on serialization.
wouldn't we get here only if source gen did something wrong? this check makes sense if we plan to make SerializeHandler public but otherwise I'd stick with always throwing

This is the root cause of the bug. Essentially, calling `EnsureConfigured()` on a fast-path only JsonTypeInfo would result in it throwing here. This PR changes it so that any exceptions are delayed until serialization/deserialization occurs (via a check on `MetadataSerializationNotSupported`)

Not directly related to the fix, but this applies a performance optimization similar to the root serialization methods. `is JsonTypeInfo<T>` checks are expensive so we prefer to guard them with checks that the handler does indeed exist.
seems related enough to me since you're reviewing every usage
